questions.stem: In an experiment the values of two spring constants were measured as $k_{1} = (10 \pm 0.2)\ \mathrm{N/m}$ and $k_{2} = (20 \pm 0.3)\ \mathrm{N/m}$. If these springs are connected in parallel, then the percentage error in equivalent spring constant is :
questions.solution:
In parallel combination $k = k_{1} + k_{2}$
$\Rightarrow k = (10 + 20) \pm (0.2 + 0.3)$
$\Rightarrow k = 30 \pm 0.5$
$\Rightarrow k = 30 \pm 1.67\%$

questions.stem:
A 4 kg mass moves under the influence of a force $\vec{F} = \left(4t^{3}\hat{i} - 3t\hat{j}\right)N$ where t is the time in second.
If mass starts from origin at $t = 0$, the velocity and position after $t = 2$ s will be :
questions.solution:
$\vec{F} = 4t^{3}\hat{i} - 3t\hat{j}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{a} = t^{3}\hat{i} - \frac{3t}{4}\hat{j}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{v} = \frac{t^{4}}{4}\hat{i} - \frac{3t^{2}}{8}\hat{j}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{r} = \frac{t^{5}}{20}\hat{i} - \frac{t^{3}}{8}\hat{j}$
$\therefore \vec{v}(t = 2) = 4\hat{i} - \frac{3}{2}\hat{j}$
and $\vec{r}(t = 2) = \frac{8}{5}\hat{i} - \hat{j}$

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.stem:
A uniform rod of mass m and length $l$ suspended by means of two identical inextensible light strings as shown in figure. Tension in one string immediately after the other string is cut, is ___________.
(g acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
about A
$mg\left(\frac{\ell}{2}\right) = \frac{m\ell^{2}}{3}\alpha$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{3g}{2\ell}$
$\therefore a_{t}(\text{at } c) = \alpha\frac{\ell}{2} = \frac{3g}{4}$
for translatory motion
$mg - T = m\left(\frac{3g}{4}\right)$
$\Rightarrow T = \frac{mg}{4}$

questions.stem:
A gas based geyser heats water flowing at the rate of 5.0 litres per minute from $27^\circ$C to 87% C. The rate of consumption of the gas is _________g/s.
(Take heat of combustion of gas $= 5.0 \times 10^{4}\ \mathrm{J/g}$) specific heat capacity of water $= 4200\ \mathrm{J/kg.^\circ C}$
questions.solution:
Flow rate = 5 litre per minute
$\Delta T = 60\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$
$\therefore \Delta Q$ (reqd.) $= 5 \times 4200 \times 60 = 1260000$ J/min.
$\Rightarrow \frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{1260000}{60} = 21000$ J/sec.
$\because \frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{dm}{dt} \times$ heat of combination
$\therefore \frac{dm}{dt} = \frac{21000}{5 \times 10^{4}} = 0.42$ g/sec.

questions.stem: If an alpha particle with energy 7.7 MeV is bombarded on a thin gold foil, the closest distance from nucleus it can reach is _________ m. (Atomic number of gold = 79 and $\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_{0}} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ in SI units)
questions.solution:
applying conservation of M.E
$7.7\ \mathrm{MeV} = \frac{q_{1}q_{2}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}r}$
$\Rightarrow 7.7 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} = \frac{2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 79 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{r} \times 9 \times 10^{9}$
$\Rightarrow r = 2.95 \times 10^{-14}$ m

questions.stem: A point charge of $10^{-8}$ C is placed at origin. The work done in moving a point charge $2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ from point A(4, 4, 2) m to B (2, 2, 1) m is ___________ J. ($\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_{0}} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ in SI units)
questions.solution:
Initial distance $= \sqrt{4^{2} + 4^{2} + 2^{2}} = 6\ \mathrm{m}$
final distance $= \sqrt{2^{2} + 2^{2} + 1^{2}} = 3\ \mathrm{m}$
$\therefore$ work done $= kq_{1}q_{2}\left(\frac{1}{r_{2}} - \frac{1}{r_{1}}\right)$
$= \frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 10^{-8} \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}{6}$
$= 30 \times 10^{-6}$ J

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.stem: A light wave described by $E = 60\,[\sin(3 \times 10^{15})t + \sin(12 \times 10^{15})t]$ (in SI units) falls on a metal surface of work function 2.8 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectron is (approximately) _______ eV. ($h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}$ J.s. and $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C)
questions.solution:
Photon with $\omega = 12 \times 10^{15}$ will have more energy
$\therefore k_{max} = h\nu - \phi$
$= \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 12 \times 10^{15}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 2\pi}\ \mathrm{eV} - 2.8\ \mathrm{eV}$
$= 7.88 - 2.8\ \mathrm{eV} \simeq 5.1\ \mathrm{eV}$

questions.stem: A current carrying solenoid is placed vertically and a particle of mass m with charge Q is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If g is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration (a) of the charged particle will satisfy:
questions.solution: The magnetic field is opposite to direction of motion of charge so magnetic force is zero. It will only experience gravitational force and move with acceleration g.

questions.stem: In a double slit experiment the distance between the slits is 0.1 cm and the screen is placed at 50 cm from the slits plane. When one slit is covered with a transparent sheet having thickness t and refractive index $n(= 1.5)$, the central fringe shifts by 0.2 cm. The value of t is _____________ cm.
questions.solution:
Shift y of fringe pattern is given by
$(\mu - 1)t = \frac{yd}{D}$
$\Rightarrow t = \frac{0.2 \times 0.1}{50 \times 0.5} = 8 \times 10^{-4}$ cm

questions.stem: The given circuit works as:

Two strings (A, B) having linear densities $\mu_{A} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{kg/m}$ and, $\mu_{B} = 4 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{kg/m}$ and lengths $L_{A} = 2.5$ m and $L_{B} = 1.5$ m respectively are joined. Free ends of A and B are tied to two rigid supports C and D, respectively creating a tension of 500 N in the wire. Two identical pulses, sent from C and D ends, take time $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$, respectively, to reach the joint. The ratio $t_{1}/t_{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
$\because V = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{V_{A}}{V_{B}} = \sqrt{\frac{\mu_{B}}{\mu_{A}}} = \sqrt{2}$
$\because t = \frac{\ell}{V}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}} = \frac{\ell_{A}}{\ell_{B}}\frac{V_{B}}{V_{A}} = \frac{2.5}{1.5\sqrt{2}} \simeq 1.18$

questions.stem: A parallel plate capacitor has capacitance C, when there is vacuum within the parallel plates. A sheet having thickness $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ of the separation between the plates and relative permittivity K is introduced between the plates. The new capacitance of the system is:
questions.solution:
$C = \frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{d}$
After inserting plate
$C^{1} = \frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{\frac{2d}{3} + \frac{d}{3K}} = \frac{3KC}{2K + 1}$

questions.stem: A 1 m long metal rod AB completes the circuit as shown in figure. The area of circuit is perpendicular to the magnetic field of 0.10 T. If the resistance of the total circuit is $2\ \Omega$ then the force needed to move the rod towards right with constant speed ($v$) of 1.5 m/s is ______________ N.
questions.solution:
Induced emf $\varepsilon = Blv = 0.15$ V
Power $= \frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{R} = 0.01125$ W
$\because P = FV \Rightarrow F = \frac{0.01125}{1.5} = 7.5 \times 10^{-3}$ N

questions.stem: A conducting circular loop of area $1.0\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$ is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies as $B = \sin(100\,t)$ Tesla. If the resistance of the loop is $100\ \Omega$, then the average thermal energy dissipated in the loop in one period is ______________ J.
questions.solution:
Flux $\phi = BA = \sin(100t)$
induced emf $\varepsilon = \frac{d\phi}{dt} = 100\cos(100t)$
power $P = \frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{R} = 100\cos^{2}(100t)$
average power $p_{avg} = 100\langle\cos^{2}(100t)\rangle = 100 \times \frac{1}{2} = 50\ \mathrm{W}$
in one rotation energy dissipated $= 50 \times T$
$= 50 \times \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \pi\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.stem: Water flows through a horizontal tube as shown in the figure. The difference in height between the water columns in vertical tubes is 5 cm and the area of cross-sections at A and B are $6\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$ and $3\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$ respectively. The rate of flow will be ___________ $\mathrm{cm^{3}/s}$. (take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
For a venturimeter
$\rho gh = \frac{1}{2}\rho\left(V_{B}^{2} - V_{A}^{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow V_{A} = \sqrt{\frac{2gh}{3}}$ $\quad \{\because V_{B} = 2V_{A}\}$
$\therefore$ volume flow rate $= V_{A}A_{A}$
$= 200\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{cm^{3}/s}$

questions.stem: Potential energy (V) versus distance (x) is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force (F) acting on a particle from high to low.
questions.solution:
Magnitude of force = magnitude of slope
$\therefore F_{BC} > F_{AB} > F_{DE} > F_{CD}$

questions.stem: An aluminium and steel rods having same lengths and cross-sections are joined to make total length of 120 cm at $30^\circ$ C. The coefficient of linear expansion of aluminium and steel are $24 \times 10^{-6}\ /^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ /^\circ\mathrm{C}$, respectively. The length of this composite rod when its temperature is raised to $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, is ____________ cm.
questions.solution:
Change in length $\Delta l = \Delta l_{1} + \Delta l_{2} = l_{1}\alpha_{1}\Delta T + l_{2}\alpha_{2}\Delta T$
$\Rightarrow \Delta l = 60 \times 24 \times 10^{-6} \times 70 + 60 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 70$
$\Rightarrow \Delta l = 0.15$ cm
$\therefore$ length $= 120 + 0.15 = 120.15$ cm

questions.stem:
The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by:
$E_{y} = 69\sin[0.6 \times 10^{3}x - 1.8 \times 10^{11}t]$ V/m.
The expression for magnetic field associated with this electromagnetic wave is ________ T.
questions.solution:
$\because$ wave is travelling in + x direction
& electric field is in y direction
so magnetic field is in z direction
$B_{0} = \frac{69}{3 \times 10^{8}} = 2.3 \times 10^{-7}$
$\therefore B_{z} = 2.3 \times 10^{-7}\sin(0.6 \times 10^{3}x - 1.8 \times 10^{11}t)$

questions.stem:
Initially a satellite of 100 kg is in a circular orbit of radius $1.5\ R_{E}$. This satellite can be moved to a circular orbit of radius $3\ R_{E}$ by supplying $\alpha \times 10^{6}$ J of energy. The value of $\alpha$ is ___________.
(Take Radius of Earth $R_{E} = 6 \times 10^{6}$ m and $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
Initial energy of satellite $= \frac{-GMm}{2 \times 1.5R} = \frac{-GMm}{3R}$
Final energy of satellite $= \frac{-GMm}{2 \times 3R} = \frac{-GMm}{6R}$
Change in energy $= \frac{-GMm}{6R} + \frac{GMm}{3R} = \frac{GMm}{6R}$
$= \frac{mgR}{6} = 10^{9}$ J
$\therefore \alpha = 1000$

questions.stem:
Consider a modified Bernoulli equation.
$$\left(P + \frac{A}{Bt^{2}}\right) + \rho g(h + Bt) + \frac{1}{2}\rho V^{2} = \text{constant}$$
If t has the dimension of time then the dimensions of A and B are _________, _________ respectively.
questions.solution:
Bt has dimensions of height h
$\therefore [B] = [M^{0}L^{1}T^{-1}]$
also $\frac{A}{Bt^{2}}$ has dimensions of pressure P
$\Rightarrow [A] = [PBt^{2}] = [M^{1}L^{0}T^{-1}]$

questions.stem: A collimated beam of light of diameter 2 mm is propagating along x-axis. The beam is required to be expanded in a collimated beam of diameter 14 mm using a system of two convex lenses. If first lens has focal length 40 mm, then the focal length of second lens is _____________ mm.
questions.solution:
$\because \tan\theta = \frac{d_{1}}{f_{1}} = \frac{d_{2}}{f_{2}}$
$\Rightarrow f_{2} = 280$ mm

questions.stem: In a microscope the objective is having focal length $f_{o} = 2$ cm and eye-piece is having focal length $f_{e} = 4$ cm. The tube length is 32 cm. The magnification produced by this microscope for normal adjustment is _________________.
questions.solution: $\because m = \frac{LD}{f_{0}f_{e}} = \frac{32 \times 25}{2 \times 4} = 100$

questions.stem:
10 mole of oxygen is heated at constant volume from $30\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $40\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The change in the internal energy of the gas is ___________ cal.
(The molecular specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure, $C_{p} = 7\ \mathrm{cal/mol.^\circ C}$ and $R = 2\ \mathrm{cal./mol.^\circ C}$.)
questions.solution:
Change in internal energy
$\Delta U = nC_{V}\Delta T = 10 \times 5 \times 10$ Cal
$= 500$ Cal

questions.stem: The heat generated in 1 minute between points A and B in the given circuit, when a battery of 9 V with internal resistance of $1\ \Omega$ is connected across these points is _____________ J.
questions.solution:
It is a balanced wheat stone bridge
$\therefore R_{eq} = 2\Omega$
$\because I = \frac{\varepsilon}{2 + r} = 3\mathrm{A}$
$\therefore P = 3^{2} \times 2 = 18$ W
$\therefore$ Heat generated (1 min.) $= 18 \times 60$
$= 1080$ J

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.stem: Two identical thin rods of mass M kg and length L m are connected as shown in figure. Moment of inertia of the combined rod system about an axis passing through point P and perpendicular to the plane of the rods is $\frac{x}{12}ML^{2}\ \mathrm{kg\ m^{2}}$. The value of x is _______________.
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia $= \left[\frac{m\ell^{2}}{3} + \left(\frac{m\ell^{2}}{12} + m\ell^{2}\right)\right]$
$= \frac{17m\ell^{2}}{12}$
